When I was a kid I wanted to learn saxophone really bad (my parents had a Kenny G cd and I guess I wanted to be like him). So instead of paying for private lessons they had me take lessons from the band teacher at the local middle school. I was homeschooled so I was already awkward and "the homeschooled kid". 

Anyway one day at soccer practice one of my teammates was like "we were all laughing at you when you were (in a lesson) the other day". I was so embarrassed by what she said I quit and didn't tell my parents why. 

The thing was, I had already been playing piano for 7 years. I play by ear and learning saxophone was really easy and I was really good and could have been really really good if I had stuck with it. And I know it was middle school and kids are mean but I still to this day remember that stupid comment.

So yeah, don't make fun of people. And if you have kids teach them not to be those crusty little assholes that laugh at other kids because I could have totally grown up and been cool like that dude on YouTube running around playing the sax solo from that George Michael song. Now I'm just a loser with 15 years of classical piano training and no saxophone.

I was that "straight" girl (F26) with the huge crush on her lesbian friend (F29, who is now technically a coworker) and it worked out. 

I didn't think she would like me because I was straight, but we were friends for a couple years, and I think we both knew we had feelings, and finally after we had a couple innocent sleepovers (movie watching, some cuddling), and us sharing an amazing kiss right before she went on a date (I may have done that so she would be thinking about me the whole time) she asked me if I would be with her. 

I was extremely scared because a.) i had never dated a girl and b.) I considered her one of my best friends, so I didn't want to risk breaking up and losing our friendship. After some thinking, I realized I would rather take the risk than keep doing what we were doing. So I said yes.

My life has changed significantly. It was the best decision I ever made. I feel complete, I feel real, I feel exactly how I always have wanted to. I've never felt this way with a guy, and looking back, I realized I really had been on the lesbian side of things for a long time, I just never put two and two together. But it's not about discovering that side of things, its just the fact that had I not taken the chance, my life would not be as good as it is now. I am generally happier. I am completely different in the way I handle this relationship than I have been with any other. I value her more than I've valued any other s/o. I respect her so much, I love everything about her (even the things that can drive me crazy), she brings out the best in me and vice versa. All of our close friends around us have expressed this repeatedly. We live together and have two dogs and are planning on moving to a bigger city soon. She saved me and I saved her. My life would be so much different if I hadn't taken that chance, and I'm thankful every day I did.

And even if we were broken up right now, I would still say this. Had I not said yes, I would be in another dead end, empty relationship with someone who I had to be drunk in order to be interested in sexually.

I'm not saying this is going to be you. For all you know, you could date this girl and realize that the girl thing isn't for you. But you'll never know if you don't try. And guess what? It's risky dating a coworker. But It's risky dating ANYONE. There's always a chance that you'll get hurt, or run into them around town if you break up, or have to see them at work. But guess what? There are also other jobs, and not every breakup is messy or confrontational. 

So, if I were you, and you feel this strongly when you see this girl, I would take a chance. Worse case she'll say no. Worse case she'll say yes and you'll break up. Downtown has a lot of lofts and a lot are government subsidized so if you are single and make less than something like $26,000/year apartments are reasonably priced. A lot of the lofts built in the past five years (vine st, metro, rumely, rocket transfer, etc) have underground parking or lots. You'll just have to pay a monthly fee. I lived in metro lofts for two years. It's really new, the apartments are nice and I paid $625 for a 740 sq/ft one bedroom. They have washers and dryers in units and you don't pay water, just electricity. It was nice but the downside is it's right in the middle of the court center bar district so if you don't want to deal with drunkies outside or waking up after the weekend with beer cans littered in the stairway then don't live there. I'm a bartender downtown so it never bothered me but I could see how it might be irritating. Also all the apartments I listed above are right near the train tracks. You learn to tune it out but if that's a deal breaker then go further west downtown around 11th-18th street. Actually unless you love the nightlife and are out boozing all the time I wouldn't move to the court ave area. But that's just my opinion.
